recoveryGaps.why: Archiving a project revokes its API keys in the same transaction and the developer console offers no unarchive, so an archived project stays listed read-only with its usage history.
recoveryGaps.fix: An unarchive action beside archive in the developer projects route that clears archived_at; the revoked keys stay revoked and new keys are created for the project.

recoveryGaps.why: A message variant is withdrawn by the thread route and the surface offers no undo, so the soft delete is only a tombstone the thread walk skips.
recoveryGaps.fix: A restore endpoint beside the conversation restore route, clearing deleted_at for one message id the caller owns.

recoveryGaps.why: Deleting a project sets deleted_at and no surface clears it, so a project deleted by accident is unreachable until an operator edits the row.
recoveryGaps.fix: A restore route beside the conversation one, and a trash listing that reads deleted_at is not null.

recoveryGaps.why: is_archived is written when a project is archived and nothing writes it back to false.
recoveryGaps.fix: Unarchive in the same route that archives, the way the conversation bulk route already does.

recoveryGaps.why: A withdrawn knowledge file keeps its row and its object for as long as the account lives; only account erasure removes it.
recoveryGaps.fix: Extend the deleted-media purge cron to knowledge files, with the same window.

recoveryGaps.why: An artifact is withdrawn with deleted_at and no route clears it.
recoveryGaps.fix: A restore route, or a documented decision that artifact deletion is immediate and the column should go.

recoveryGaps.why: A deleted memory keeps its row forever so the sync tombstone stays readable by an offline device; nothing ever collects it once every device has seen it.
recoveryGaps.fix: A tombstone collector that deletes rows whose is_deleted is true and whose updated_at is older than the longest sync window.

recoveryGaps.why: The gateway compatibility table mirrors the chat completions API and carries no product surface of its own.
recoveryGaps.fix: Restore reaches it through the web_conversations restore route once the compatibility mirror is folded in.

recoveryGaps.why: The gateway compatibility table has no retention sweep of its own; its rows go with the account.
recoveryGaps.fix: Include it in the retention sweep that already collects web_conversations.

recoveryGaps.why: The gateway compatibility table carries is_archived for wire parity and no surface writes it.
recoveryGaps.fix: Drop the column, or mirror the archive write from web_conversations.

recoveryGaps.why: A developer session is archived when its work ends and the surface offers no way back to the active list.
recoveryGaps.fix: Clear archived_at from the session route that sets it.

recoveryGaps.why: An archived flag definition is retired deliberately; bringing it back would resurrect a rollout nobody is watching.
recoveryGaps.fix: Define a new flag instead, or add an explicit unarchive with an audit event.

recoveryGaps.why: Archiving a developer project revokes its keys in the same request and is one-way by design, as OpenAI project archiving is; an unarchive would bring back a spend scope whose keys no longer work.
recoveryGaps.fix: Create a new project instead, or add an explicit unarchive that issues no key back and records an audit event.

derived-index.why: A retrieval document is a copy of the resource made searchable; a delete that stops at the original leaves the copy findable.

embeddings.why: A vector is the resource in a form a model can still recall, so it goes when the resource does.

caches.why: A cached body outlives the row it was derived from unless the delete reaches it, and a TTL is not a deletion.

scheduled-work.why: Work queued against a deleted resource wakes up, finds nothing, and either fails forever or acts on a stale copy.

shared-links.why: A link handed to somebody else is the one thing a delete cannot leave working.

audit-trail.why: The record that something happened is what survives the thing itself; erasure may not rewrite it.
